title: SAYING GOODBYE
author: Dola Dutta Roy
text:
She was sinking.
Deep inside her belly,
Fear rose like the creeper around a tree.
The Virus had stolen her Mom who died
In a hospital bed.
Alone.
All those comforting words,
Were not sung,
All those moments of saying goodbye,
Festered like wounds instead inside.
She tightened her grip on the umbrella
That shaded her young face, and sighed.
Like the feathery touch of a bird in your bosom,
The sun above
Bathed her fragile frame.
She let it burn her
To soak in her sorrow,
And looked around.
In her fractured reality
Nothing had changed.
Everything was just the same.
The sky still remained blue.
Fresh leaves emerged
From the remains of dying plants, and waved,
Unmoved, unperturbed.
The radios played the same songs
and the street dogs
Still chased their own shadows.
She took some faltering steps,
And then
With magic in her fingers,
And fire in her eyes,
she began to stitch her dreams back again
Before it was too late.
Before she could shed
One last drop of tear.
